items.title: NLM: Acid Jazz & 90s Crossover 2026-03-17
items.description: Acid jazz is a UK hybrid of American soul music that incorporates 1970s influences with a distinct electronic twist [1]. It emerged strongly in the 1990s alongside hip hop, bridging older generations who loved jazz with younger crowds who loved electronic music [1, 2]. The genre frequently featured live bands performing alongside DJs, creating a crossover configuration that bubbled up from the underground to the mainstream [1, 3].
items.quote: Acid jazz, the UK hybrid of American soul music, started to resonate here in the States... this sound was reminiscent of 1970s influences but with a new electronic twist [1].
items.quote_source: King Britt, Organised Sound, Volume 27, Issue 1 [1, 4]

items.title: NLM: Deep Focus IDM 2026-03-16
items.description: This playlist harnesses the intricate rhythms and atmospheric synthesizers of IDM to maintain momentum and clarity during deep work sessions. Rooted in the electronic experimentation and vibrant scenes discussed by King Britt, these instrumental tracks provide an immersive, forward-moving soundscape. The music balances energetic drive with analytical structure to perfectly power your cognitive focus throughout a busy Monday. Requested as a focused Monday work playlist with no vocals.

items.title: NLM: Acid Jazz Essentials 2026-03-16
items.description: Acid jazz emerged in the 1990s as a vibrant UK hybrid of American soul music that incorporated a new electronic twist [1]. The genre successfully bridged generations by bringing together older jazz enthusiasts and younger hip hop fans in a unique cultural crossover [2]. It frequently featured innovative live configurations, such as live bands performing alongside DJs, which helped change the landscape of club music [1].
items.quote: Acid jazz, the UK hybrid of American soul music, started to resonate here in the States.
items.quote_source: King Britt in 'We Cross Examine with Old Sonic DNA' [1]

items.title: NLM: Acid Jazz & 90s Grooves 2026-03-15
items.description: Acid jazz emerged in the 1990s as a UK hybrid of American soul music that brought a new electronic twist to 1970s influences. The genre fostered crossover success by bridging generations, uniting older jazz enthusiasts with younger hip hop fans. It also pioneered new live configurations by seamlessly blending traditional live bands with DJs on stage.
items.quote: Acid jazz, the UK hybrid of American soul music, started to resonate here in the States... this sound was reminiscent of 1970s influences but with a new electronic twist.

items.title: Codex: Basslines for Difficult People
items.description: Mutant disco and post-punk-funk from the 1979-1983 corridor where no-wave abrasion, dub space, disco momentum, and bass-first minimalism all started speaking the same language. Built around tracks with enough critical or artist commentary to support a quote-backed playlist email.

items.title: Sonnet: Rust and Blue — A Rothko Meditation
items.description: Inspired by Mark Rothko's *No. 61 (Rust and Blue)* (1953). Ambient, neo-classical, and drone music that mirrors the painting's luminous stillness, emotional weight, and tension between warm rust and cool blue. Sent to randycounsman@gmail.com with painting image and per-track explanations.

items.title: Sonnet: Delta Shadows — Obscure Architects of the Blues
items.description: The unheralded pioneers who built the blues — artists so influential that everyone knows their sound but almost no one knows their name. Pre-war Delta and city blues from artists who shaped Robert Johnson, Muddy Waters, and everything that followed. 12 tracks.

items.title: Sonnet: Bad Brains Adjacent — Best of the Billing
items.description: 36 bands that shared a documented concert bill with Bad Brains, each represented by their signature track. Source: ChatGPT conversation using Concert Archives data.

items.title: Codex: Velvet Traffic
items.description: A warm, left-field groove travelogue for a listener whose taste already jumps from post-punk and jazz to Japanese music and deep catalog discovery. Ethiopian jazz, Brazilian psych-funk, synth-soul, downtown minimalism, and late-night city-pop glow all sit in the same lane here.

items.title: Sonnet: Tokyo Burning
items.description: Japanese punk, hardcore, and no-wave from the 80s and 90s. Spans Blue Hearts pop-punk to GISM noise-metal to Shonen Knife power-pop to Boredoms chaos.

items.title: Sonnet: Orange and Yellow
items.description: Inspired by Mark Rothko's *Orange and Yellow* (1956) — warm, luminous, meditative color field painting. Ambient, spiritual jazz, neo-classical, and drone for deep listening.

items.title: Sonnet: New Horizons
items.description: Discovery playlist — all new artists, zero overlap with existing library. Inspired by existing taste across post-punk, soul, hip-hop, jazz, and experimental.
